events.ai_basis: Using this framework, we resolve an open problem in commutative algebra and formally verify the resulting proof in Lean 4 with essentially no human involvement.

why: The only post-snapshot event that touches the statement is Gille–Izquierdo–Lucchini Arteche (Jan 2025): H¹(K,G)=1 for complete discretely valued fields of dimension 2. That is one class of fields, so it is a case. It is unreviewed and credible: the authors are established specialists, and no doubt specific to the paper is recorded. The class is not empty of new perfect instances: a perfect characteristic-0 K can have an imperfect residue field, and the paper removes exactly that perfect-residue assumption. Nguyen 2026 proves things about pseudo-semisimple groups, which the statement does not ask about, and an equivalence with a generalised conjecture. On semisimple groups it adds nothing new, so it is a variant. Lourdeaux–Zidani is about Conjecture I, so it is a variant. Ju et al. resolve a commutative-algebra problem and have nothing on Serre II, so its scope is none. Its AI role (generated) is recorded from its own quote but does not bear on this problem. Izquierdo–Lucchini Arteche 2023 is before the snapshot (v3 is the accepted version, with no new mathematics shown). It is a reduction, so its scope is none; the journal acceptance makes it digested. The classical results before the snapshot are each cases. None of them is whole. Kneser has no date, but every source treats it as long-known prior work, so I placed it before the snapshot.
doubts: Wikipedia's claim that the conjecture is 'proven for all groups over all perfect fields' has no source and is contradicted by the 2023–2026 specialist papers, so I did not credit it. Verification of the pre-snapshot classical journal results rests on secondary citations; none was opened. Kneser's date is unknown. Nguyen was read only at abstract level.
